topic: Qwen decode jump, further speed levers, own-backend question

qwen_decode_jump_explained.old_finding: b10472 Vulkan, q8_0/q8_0 at ctx 262144: 20-23 t/s with MTP
qwen_decode_jump_explained.new_measurement: b10902 Vulkan (411+ builds newer) and a rebuilt current-master Vulkan: 52.6 t/s chat_code
qwen_decode_jump_explained.cause: upstream Vulkan progress between b10472 and b10902, plus q8_0/q8_0 now allocating at 262k. Not a model/config trick. MTP n4 was already in the old config.
qwen_decode_jump_explained.not_the_cause: no change to weights, KV type, prompt, or sampling

qwen_sweep_262k_mmproj_newmaster_vulkan.conclusion: q4_0/q4_0 KV frees ~3.1 GiB at identical decode. draft-mtp-adaptive adds ~1.3-2.7 t/s on chat_explain only, and is slightly less stable on code. Ceiling for code is ~52-53 t/s.

mtp_plus_ngram_q8q8.note: the 280-353 t/s reps are a cross-request ngram-cache artifact from identical temperature-0 requests; first rep is 70. Not a real gain.

bonsai_sweep_262k_rocm_mtp_build.conclusion: q4_0/q4_0 KV frees ~3.9 GiB at the same decode. MTP n2 (~70/57) beats DFlash2 at every depth tested. No further llama.cpp lever found.

own_backend.to_go_faster_no: both models are now speculation-limited; llama.cpp MTP integration is the ceiling. Config + KV choice is all that remains.
own_backend.to_go_much_faster: yes, but adopt rather than write: ZINC (Vulkan+ROCm, 1 R9700, ~7-8% decode + up to 1.9x prefill over llama.cpp), or the vLLM radiance fork (single R9700 MXFP4+MTP, 137.7 t/s, needs MXFP4/FP8 weights). NInfer is CUDA-only sm_120a.
own_backend.from_scratch: 6+ months; not worth it for a single card when ZINC exists.
